s: 1925, Milwaukee America Kalender, volume 45, Geo. Brumder, Milwaukee, page 20
Man and woman get married, so both possess certain property, even when this is only clothes.

Mann.et: From Middle High German man, from Old High German man, from Proto-West Germanic *mann, from Proto-Germanic *mann-, from Proto-Indo-European *mon-. Doublet of man.

Mannequin.et: Borrowed from French mannequin, from Dutch manneken.

männlich.et: From Middle High German manlich, from Old High German manlīh, manalīh, from Proto-West Germanic *mannlīk, from Proto-Germanic *mannlīkaz. By surface analysis, Mann + lich. Cognates include Dutch mannelijk, English manly, and Old Norse mannligr (“human”) (whenc…

s: a male animal or a male plant
a trick that dogs or other quadrupeds do, consisting of resting on their hind legs with an upright body (and begging)
The dog sits up and begs.
Wenn unsere Mannschaft so weiterspielt, werden wir bestimmt gewinnen!
If our team keeps playing like this, we will definitely win!
They are the very best teams
group of soldiers belonging to one military unit
Mannschaft.et: From Middle High German manschaft; analysable as Mann (“man”) + -schaft (“-hood, -ship”). Compare English manship.

s: the national football team of Germany
Mannschaft.et: Partly from etymology 1 above, partly a reborrowing from other European languages including French la Mannschaft (“the German national football team”). While the national squad has always been referred to as die Mannschaft in German, this used to mean no more …

s: any plant of the genus Androsace

mannigfaltig.et: From Middle High German manecvaltec, from Old High German manicfaltīg, from Proto-Germanic *managafalþaz, equivalent to manch + faltig. Compare English manifold.

s: a municipality of Upper Austria, Austria
Mannheim (an independent city in Baden-Württemberg, Germany)
One of the four districts of the Grand Duchy of Baden
Mannheim.et: From Old High German Mannenheim, from the given name Manno + heim (“home”).

s: 1842, Des Wagnergesellen E. Ch. Döbel: Wanderungen im Morgenlande (published by Ludwig Storch), volume 1, page 178
Like the men, the women also bathe daily in their own bathing areas, which no male foot is allowed to enter.
Mannheimer (native or inhabitant of the city of Mannheim, Baden-Württemberg, Germany) (usually male)

Männlein.et: From Middle High German menlīn, mennelīn, from Old High German menlīn, mennilīn, mannilīn, equivalent to Mann + -lein. Compare English manling.

s: »[…]Der Mann muß sich unabhängig halten; er hat seine eigenen Mannesangelegenheiten. Der Mann muß mannhaft sein«, sagte Oblonski und öffnete das Tor.
" […] A man must be independent; he has his masculine interests. A man has to be manly," said Oblonsky, opening the door.
mannhaft.et: From Middle High German manhaft. Equivalent to Mann + -haft.

mannigfach.et: From Middle High German manecvach; equivalent to manch + -fach.

mannstoll.et: Contraction of Middle High German mannes tol. Equivalent to Manns + toll.

s: 1545, Martin Luther, Luther Bible, Genesis 2:23 (with KJV translation)
And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.

Mannweib.et: Calque of Ancient Greek ἀνδρόγυνος (andrógunos), Mann + Weib.

s: team selection, team side, team lineup (sports, politics etc.)

männiglich.et: Middle High German mannegelīch, Old High German mannogilīh, from man (“man”) and welih (“which”).

Mannomann.et: Univerbation of Mann + oh + Mann, an emphatic repetition of the interjection Mann (“(Oh) man!”).

s: man, male (often with the connotation of being strong, handsome or manly)
1901, Max Henning, Der Koran, 2:282 (with Yusuf Ali's translation)
and if there are not two men, then a man and two women, such as ye choose, for witnesses, so that if one of them errs, the other can remind her.

manly, masculine (said e.g. of a woman or an overly macho man)
männisch.et: From Mann + -isch. Compare the also pejorative weibisch, kindisch. Doublet of Mensch.
